subproblems.title: Hⁿ of a disc in an n-dimensional linear subspace equals ω_nρⁿ (reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim Q = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n), let y ∈ Q and ρ > 0. Then H^n(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n), where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → y ∈ Q → 0 < ρ → μHE[n] ((Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball y ρ) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.integer_density_tangent_planes-a1.two_dim_cone_density-a1.subspace_ball_measure-a1, status accepted, candidate commit a029156d2b71053da5c6d27b9abcc46011c9cfac), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. It is the sibling subspace_ball already cited by the supplied proof of cbr_ci_cp_invariant_measure_product ("Hⁿ(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_nρⁿ for an n-dimensional subspace Q, y ∈ Q, ρ > 0, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n"). In this split it is used by rectangle_formula (the normalization Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n) and by product_of_rectangles (Hⁿ(V ∩ B_j(0)) = ω_n jⁿ < ∞ for the finite-measure cover). Its accepted natural proof is reproduced verbatim below; there, "the parent proof" refers to that node's original parent in the dimension-reduction branch:
Source: the conventions of the parent proof ("For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q"), proved here in every dimension n.
1. Let ι : Q → ℝ^P be the inclusion x ↦ (x : ℝ^P). It is an isometry, because the norm of Q is the restriction of the norm of ℝ^P, and its range is Q. By Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage, μHE[n](ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y))) = μHE[n](B_ρ(y) ∩ Q), where the left side is the measure μHE[n] of the metric space Q. Also B_ρ(y) ∩ Q = Q ∩ B_ρ(y).
2. Let y₀ := ⟨y, hy⟩ ∈ Q. Since the distance of Q is the restriction of the distance of ℝ^P, ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y)) = B_ρ(y₀), the open ball of Q.
3. Q is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with finrank ℝ Q = n. By Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (μHE[finrank ℝ Q] = volume on Q, the volume of measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace), rewritten with finrank ℝ Q = n, the measure μHE[n] of Q equals volume.
4. volume on Q is an additive Haar measure, so Mathlib Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos (ρ > 0) gives volume(B_ρ(y₀)) = ofReal(ρ^{finrank ℝ Q})·volume(B_1(0_Q)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·volume(B_1(0_Q)).
5. Let b be stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q reindexed by Fin n (possible since finrank ℝ Q = n) and e := b.repr : Q ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) = Euclid n. By Mathlib LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving, e is measure preserving for the volumes; as e is a linear isometry equivalence, B_1(0_Q) = e⁻¹(B_1(0)) with B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n. Hence volume(B_1(0_Q)) = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) = unitBallVolume n.
6. Combining steps 1–5: μHE[n](Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = μHE[n](B_ρ(y₀)) = volume(B_ρ(y₀)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n). The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0, where Q = {0}. ∎
proof_key_steps: The inclusion of Q is an isometry, so μHE[n](Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) is μHE[n] of the ball B_ρ(y) of Q.
On the n-dimensional inner product space Q, μHE[n] = volume.
A linear isometry Q ≃ Euclid n preserves volume, so volume(B_1(0_Q)) = ω_n.

subproblems.title: A locally finite measure carried by an n-dimensional subspace V and invariant under translations by V is a constant multiple of Hⁿ⌞V
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), and let m be a Borel measure on ℝ^P such that m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, m(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and m({x : v + x ∈ A}) = m(A) for every v ∈ V and every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P. Then there is c ∈ [0, ∞] with m = c·(Hⁿ⌞V), i.e. m(A) = c·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (m : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → m (V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → m K < ∞) → (∀ v ∈ V, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → m ((fun x => v + x) ⁻¹' A) = m A) → ∃ c : ℝ≥0∞, m = c • (μHE[n]).restrict (V : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2(b)–(c) of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_cp_invariant_measure_product (coordinates on V, translation invariance of the pushed-down measure, uniqueness of Haar measure), stated here for a measure that is already carried by V. The coordinate space ℝⁿ of that step 1 is replaced by V itself (an n-dimensional real inner product space, isometric to ℝⁿ): the orthogonal projection onto V plays the role of π and the inclusion of V plays the role of L.
Notation: V also denotes the subtype ↥V with the restricted norm, inner product, topology and Borel σ-algebra; it is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, hence a locally compact, second countable topological additive group. ι : V → ℝ^P is the inclusion, π := V.orthogonalProjectionOnto : ℝ^P → V is the orthogonal projection onto V (continuous linear), and vol_V is the volume of V (Mathlib measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace), an additive Haar measure on V.
1. (Reduction.) Since n = finrank ℝ V, substitute n := finrank ℝ V.
2. (Elementary facts.) ι is an isometry (isometry_subtype_coe) with range V. π(ι w) = w for w ∈ V (Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self); hence, by linearity of π, π(ι w + x) = w + π(x) for w ∈ V and x ∈ ℝ^P, and ι(π x) = x for every x ∈ V. Both ι and π are continuous, hence Borel measurable.
3. (Invariance as an identity of measures.) For v ∈ V, (x ↦ v + x)_# m = m: for Borel A, ((v + ·)_# m)(A) = m((v + ·)⁻¹(A)) = m(A) by Measure.map_apply (translation is measurable) and the invariance hypothesis; equality of the measures follows by Measure.ext.
4. (The pushed-down measure is translation invariant.) Let m' := π_# m, a Borel measure on V. For g ∈ V we have (g + ·) ∘ π = π ∘ (ι g + ·) by step 2, so by Measure.map_map and step 3 with v = ι g ∈ V: (g + ·)_# m' = ((g + ·) ∘ π)_# m = (π ∘ (ι g + ·))_# m = π_#((ι g + ·)_# m) = π_# m = m'. Thus m' is additive-left-invariant (Measure.IsAddLeftInvariant).
5. (m' is finite on compact sets.) Let K ⊆ V be compact (hence closed in the Hausdorff space V, hence Borel). Then π⁻¹(K) ⊆ ι(K) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ V): if x ∈ π⁻¹(K) and x ∈ V, then x = ι(π x) with π x ∈ K. Hence m'(K) = m(π⁻¹(K)) ≤ m(ι(K)) + m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = m(ι(K)) < ∞, because ι(K) is compact (continuous image of a compact set) and m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0. So m' is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts).
6. (Uniqueness of Haar measure.) By steps 4–5 and Mathlib Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul, applied to m' and the additive Haar measure vol_V, m' = c₀·vol_V with c₀ := m'.addHaarScalarFactor vol_V ∈ [0, ∞). Put c := c₀, regarded as an element of [0, ∞].
7. (m is the image of m'.) ι ∘ π agrees with the identity on V and m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, so ι ∘ π = id m-almost everywhere. Hence (Measure.map_id, Measure.map_congr, Measure.map_map) m = id_# m = (ι ∘ π)_# m = ι_#(π_# m) = ι_# m'.
8. (The image of vol_V is Hⁿ⌞V.) By Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, the Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[finrank ℝ V] of the inner product space V equals vol_V. Since ι is an isometry with range V, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives ι_#(μHE[n] of V) = μHE[n]⌞(range ι) = Hⁿ⌞V.
9. (Conclusion.) By steps 6–8 and Measure.map_smul (ι is measurable): m = ι_# m' = ι_#(c·vol_V) = c·ι_#(vol_V) = c·ι_#(μHE[n] of V) = c·(Hⁿ⌞V). The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0 (V = {0}, where c = m({0})). ∎
Formalization notes (verified by a scratch compile of a complete single-theorem proof after import GMT.Ch07.Submission): obtain ⟨c, key⟩ : ∃ c : NNReal, m' = c • (volume : Measure V) from Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul (with local `have` instances for IsAddLeftInvariant m' and IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts m') before rewriting, since rewriting m' inside addHaarScalarFactor m' volume fails with a dependent motive; Submodule.orthogonalProjection_mem_subspace_eq_self is deprecated in favour of Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto_mem_subspace_eq_self; the final NNReal-versus-ℝ≥0∞ scalar comparison closes by rfl.
proof_key_steps: Push m down to V by the orthogonal projection π: m' := π_# m is translation invariant on V, because (g + ·) ∘ π = π ∘ (ι g + ·) for g ∈ V and m is V-invariant, and finite on compact sets, because π⁻¹(K) ⊆ ι(K) ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ V) and m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0.
Uniqueness of Haar measure on the finite-dimensional inner product space V gives m' = c·vol_V.
m = ι_# m' since ι ∘ π = id on V, which carries m; and ι_# vol_V = ι_#(μHE[n] of V) = Hⁿ⌞V because μHE[n] = vol_V on V and the inclusion ι is an isometry. Hence m = c·Hⁿ⌞V.

subproblems.title: Transverse measure σ on V^⊥ with ν(p⁻¹A ∩ q⁻¹B) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for a locally finite V-invariant measure ν
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n, let p := V.starProjection and q := V^⊥.starProjection be the orthogonal projections of ℝ^P onto V and onto V^⊥, and let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K and ν({x : v + x ∈ A}) = ν(A) for every v ∈ V and every Borel A. Then there is a Borel measure σ on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥) = 0, σ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, and ν({y : p y ∈ A, q y ∈ B}) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for all Borel A, B ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → (∀ v ∈ V, ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν ((fun x => v + x) ⁻¹' A) = ν A) → ∃ σ : Measure (Euclid P), σ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → σ K < ∞) ∧ ∀ A B : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → ν (V.starProjection ⁻¹' A ∩ Vᗮ.starProjection ⁻¹' B) = σ B * μHE[n] (A ∩ (V : Set (Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3 and 4 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_cp_invariant_measure_product. The coordinate measure m_B = π_#(ν⌞q⁻¹(B)) on ℝⁿ of its step 2 is replaced by m := p_#(ν⌞q⁻¹(B)) on ℝ^P, which is carried by V; for this measure, its step 2(c) together with its step 1 (Haar uniqueness and vol(L⁻¹(A)) = Hⁿ(A ∩ V)) is exactly the sibling subspace_haar. σ is the measure of its step 3. Uses the siblings subspace_haar and subspace_ball.
Notation and facts: p := V.starProjection and q := V^⊥.starProjection are continuous linear maps ℝ^P → ℝ^P, hence Borel measurable. For every y: p y ∈ V and q y ∈ V^⊥ (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem), and p y + q y = y (Submodule.starProjection_add_starProjection_orthogonal). For v ∈ V: p v = v (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff) and q v = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_apply_eq_zero), hence by linearity p(v + y) = v + p y and q(v + y) = q y. V is closed (finite-dimensional; Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and V^⊥ is closed (Submodule.isClosed_orthogonal), so V, V^⊥ and their complements are Borel. ω_n := unitBallVolume n = vol(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ) satisfies 0 < ω_n < ∞ (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). By subspace_ball (Q = V, y = 0 ∈ V, ρ = 1): Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n·ofReal(1ⁿ) = ω_n.
1. (Bounded boxes have finite ν-measure.) If E ⊆ B̄_R(0) and F ⊆ B̄_S(0), then {y : p y ∈ E, q y ∈ F} ⊆ B̄_{R+S}(0), because ‖y‖ = ‖p y + q y‖ ≤ ‖p y‖ + ‖q y‖ ≤ R + S. Since B̄_{R+S}(0) is compact, ν({y : p y ∈ E, q y ∈ F}) ≤ ν(B̄_{R+S}(0)) < ∞.
2. (Definition of σ.) Let σ := ω_n⁻¹·q_#(ν⌞p⁻¹(B_1(0))), where p⁻¹(B_1(0)) = {y : ‖p y‖ < 1}. For Borel B (Measure.smul_apply, Measure.map_apply, Measure.restrict_apply): σ(B) = ω_n⁻¹·ν(p⁻¹(B_1(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(B)).
3. (Rectangle formula for bounded B.) Fix a Borel set A and a bounded Borel set B, say B ⊆ B̄_S(0). Let m := p_#(ν⌞q⁻¹(B)); for Borel E, m(E) = ν(p⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)). We check the hypotheses of subspace_haar for m:
(a) m(ℝ^P ∖ V) = ν(p⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ V) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = ν(∅) = 0, since p y ∈ V for every y.
(b) If K is compact, then K is closed, hence Borel, and bounded, so K ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R, and m(K) = ν(p⁻¹(K) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) < ∞ by step 1.
(c) For v ∈ V and Borel E, the set (v + ·)⁻¹(E) is Borel and p⁻¹((v + ·)⁻¹(E)) ∩ q⁻¹(B) = {y : v + p y ∈ E, q y ∈ B} = {y : p(v + y) ∈ E, q(v + y) ∈ B} = (v + ·)⁻¹(p⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)). As p⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B) is Borel, the invariance of ν gives m((v + ·)⁻¹(E)) = ν(p⁻¹(E) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = m(E).
By subspace_haar (applied to P, n, m, V) there is c ∈ [0, ∞] with m = c·(Hⁿ⌞V). Evaluating at the Borel set B_1(0): ν(p⁻¹(B_1(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = m(B_1(0)) = c·Hⁿ(B_1(0) ∩ V) = c·ω_n. By step 2, σ(B) = ω_n⁻¹·(c·ω_n) = c, because ω_n⁻¹·ω_n = 1 (0 < ω_n < ∞; ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel). Therefore ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = m(A) = c·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V).
4. (σ is carried by V^⊥.) q⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥) = ∅ because q y ∈ V^⊥ for every y. Hence, by step 2, σ(ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥) = ω_n⁻¹·ν(p⁻¹(B_1(0)) ∩ ∅) = 0.
5. (σ is finite on compact sets.) Let K be compact; then K is closed, hence Borel, and bounded, say K ⊆ B̄_S(0). By step 2, σ(K) = ω_n⁻¹·ν(p⁻¹(B_1(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(K)); here ω_n⁻¹ < ∞ because ω_n > 0, and ν(p⁻¹(B_1(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(K)) < ∞ by step 1 (B_1(0) ⊆ B̄_1(0)). So σ(K) < ∞.
6. (Arbitrary Borel B.) Let A, B be Borel and, for j ∈ ℕ, B⁽ʲ⁾ := B ∩ B_j(0), where B_j(0) is the open ball of radius j about 0. Each B⁽ʲ⁾ is Borel and bounded, B⁽ʲ⁾ ⊆ B⁽ʲ⁺¹⁾, and ⋃_j B⁽ʲ⁾ = B because ⋃_j B_j(0) = ℝ^P (iUnion_ball_nat). The sets p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B⁽ʲ⁾) therefore increase with union p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B). By continuity from below (Monotone.measure_iUnion) for ν and for σ, step 3 for each B⁽ʲ⁾, and ENNReal.iSup_mul ((⨆_j a_j)·b = ⨆_j (a_j·b) in [0, ∞]): ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) = ⨆_j ν(p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B⁽ʲ⁾)) = ⨆_j σ(B⁽ʲ⁾)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) = (⨆_j σ(B⁽ʲ⁾))·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V).
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 4, 5 and 6 are the three claimed properties of σ. ∎
Formalization notes (verified by a scratch compile of a complete single-theorem proof after import GMT.Ch07.Submission): Hⁿ(B_1(0) ∩ V) = ω_n is rw [inter_comm, Submission.idtp_tdc_subspace_ball_measure P n V 0 1 hn V.zero_mem one_pos] followed by simp; the Borel set ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥ is V.isClosed_orthogonal.measurableSet.compl (note V.isClosed_orthogonal : IsClosed (Vᗮ : Set _), not Vᗮ.isClosed_orthogonal); bounded sets give closed balls by Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall.
proof_key_steps: σ := ω_n⁻¹·q_#(ν⌞{‖p y‖ < 1}) is carried by V^⊥ because q y ∈ V^⊥ for every y, and is finite on compact sets because bounded boxes {y : p y ∈ E, q y ∈ F} lie in compact balls.

For bounded Borel B, m := p_#(ν⌞q⁻¹B) is carried by V, finite on compact sets and V-invariant, so m = c·Hⁿ⌞V by subspace_haar; evaluating on B_1(0) with subspace_ball (Hⁿ(V ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n) gives c = σ(B), hence ν(p⁻¹A ∩ q⁻¹B) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V).
For arbitrary Borel B, pass to the limit along B ∩ B_j(0) by continuity from below for ν and σ and ENNReal.iSup_mul.

subproblems.title: A measure with rectangle values σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) is the image of (Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ under addition
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim V = n, let p := V.starProjection and q := V^⊥.starProjection be the orthogonal projections of ℝ^P onto V and onto V^⊥, let σ be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with σ(ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥) = 0 and σ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, and let ν be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with ν({y : p y ∈ A, q y ∈ B}) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) for all Borel A, B ⊆ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then ν(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (lower Lebesgue integral over V), i.e. ν is the image of (Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ under (t, y) ↦ t + y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν σ : Measure (Euclid P)) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → σ (Vᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → σ K < ∞) → (∀ A B : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → ν (V.starProjection ⁻¹' A ∩ Vᗮ.starProjection ⁻¹' B) = σ B * μHE[n] (A ∩ (V : Set (Euclid P)))) → ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → ν A = ∫⁻ t in (V : Set (Euclid P)), σ ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5, 6, 7 and 8 of the supplied proof of cbr_ci_cp_invariant_measure_product, with the rectangle formula of its step 4 and the properties of σ from its step 3 taken as hypotheses. Uses the sibling subspace_ball.
Notation and facts: p := V.starProjection and q := V^⊥.starProjection are continuous linear (hence Borel measurable); p y ∈ V, q y ∈ V^⊥ and p y + q y = y for every y (Submodule.starProjection_add_starProjection_orthogonal). For t ∈ V: p t = t (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff) and q t = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_apply_eq_zero). For y ∈ V^⊥: p y = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff) and q y = y. V is closed (finite-dimensional), hence Borel. ω_n := unitBallVolume n < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top).
1. (σ is σ-finite.) σ is finite on compact sets, hence locally finite on the proper space ℝ^P (isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), hence σ-finite because ℝ^P is second countable (sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite); in particular σ is s-finite, as Measure.prod_apply requires.
2. (The candidate λ.) Let s : ℝ^P × ℝ^P → ℝ^P, s(t, y) := t + y (continuous, hence measurable), and λ := s_#((Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ). For Borel A, s⁻¹(A) is Borel, and Measure.map_apply and Measure.prod_apply give λ(A) = ((Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ)(s⁻¹(A)) = ∫⁻ σ({y : (t, y) ∈ s⁻¹(A)}) d(Hⁿ⌞V)(t) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t). Hence it suffices to prove ν = λ.
3. (Rectangles form a π-system.) Let 𝒞 be the family of rectangles p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B) with A, B Borel. Each is Borel, and (p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B)) ∩ (p⁻¹(A') ∩ q⁻¹(B')) = p⁻¹(A ∩ A') ∩ q⁻¹(B ∩ B') ∈ 𝒞, so 𝒞 is a π-system.
4. (Rectangles generate the Borel σ-algebra.) Let 𝒢 be the σ-algebra generated by 𝒞. Then 𝒢 ⊆ Borel by step 3. Conversely, p is 𝒢-measurable because p⁻¹(A) = p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(ℝ^P) ∈ 𝒞 for Borel A, and q is 𝒢-measurable because q⁻¹(B) = p⁻¹(ℝ^P) ∩ q⁻¹(B) ∈ 𝒞 for Borel B. Addition ℝ^P × ℝ^P → ℝ^P is Borel measurable (ℝ^P is second countable; Measurable.add), so y ↦ p y + q y is 𝒢-measurable; this map is the identity, so every Borel set lies in 𝒢. Thus 𝒢 is the Borel σ-algebra.
5. (A countable cover by rectangles of finite ν-measure.) For j ∈ ℕ let S_j := p⁻¹(B_j(0)) ∩ q⁻¹(B_j(0)) ∈ 𝒞. These cover ℝ^P: given y, choose j ∈ ℕ with j > max(‖p y‖, ‖q y‖). By hypothesis ν(S_j) = σ(B_j(0))·Hⁿ(B_j(0) ∩ V). Here σ(B_j(0)) ≤ σ(B̄_j(0)) < ∞ (closed balls are compact), and Hⁿ(B_j(0) ∩ V) = 0 if j = 0 (the ball is empty), while for j ≥ 1 subspace_ball (Q = V, y = 0 ∈ V, ρ = j > 0) gives Hⁿ(V ∩ B_j(0)) = ω_n·ofReal(jⁿ) < ∞. Hence ν(S_j) < ∞.
6. (ν and λ agree on rectangles.) Let S = p⁻¹(A) ∩ q⁻¹(B) with A, B Borel, and fix t ∈ V. Since σ(ℝ^P ∖ V^⊥) = 0, σ(X) = σ(X ∩ V^⊥) for every X ⊆ ℝ^P (measure_inter_conull). For y ∈ V^⊥ we have p(t + y) = p t + p y = t and q(t + y) = q t + q y = y. Hence: if t ∈ A, then {y : t + y ∈ S} ∩ V^⊥ = B ∩ V^⊥, so σ({y : t + y ∈ S}) = σ(B ∩ V^⊥) = σ(B); if t ∉ A, then {y : t + y ∈ S} ∩ V^⊥ = ∅, so σ({y : t + y ∈ S}) = 0. That is, σ({y : t + y ∈ S}) = 1_A(t)·σ(B) for every t ∈ V. By step 2, setLIntegral_congr_fun (V is Borel), lintegral_indicator_const (A is Borel) and Measure.restrict_apply: λ(S) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} 1_A(t)·σ(B) dHⁿ(t) = σ(B)·(Hⁿ⌞V)(A) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) = ν(S), the last equality being the hypothesis.
7. (Conclusion.) 𝒞 is a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra (steps 3–4), the sets S_j ∈ 𝒞 cover ℝ^P and have ν(S_j) < ∞ (step 5), and ν = λ on 𝒞 (step 6). By uniqueness of measures (Mathlib Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion), ν = λ, so by step 2 ν(A) = λ(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) for every Borel A. ∎
Formalization notes (verified by a scratch compile of a complete single-theorem proof after import GMT.Ch07.Submission): a local `have : IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts σ := ⟨hσfin⟩` lets instance search supply SFinite σ for Measure.prod_apply; state the generation as (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (Euclid P)) = MeasurableSpace.generateFrom 𝒞, prove ≤ with @Measurable.add _ _ _ _ (MeasurableSpace.generateFrom 𝒞) (fun y => p y) (fun y => q y) _ hp hq and funext of Submodule.starProjection_add_starProjection_orthogonal, and ≥ with MeasurableSpace.generateFrom_le; Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff takes the submodule explicitly, e.g. (V.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff).mpr hy.
proof_key_steps: σ is σ-finite, so λ := s_#((Hⁿ⌞V) ⊗ σ) with s(t, y) = t + y satisfies λ(A) = ∫⁻_{t∈V} σ({y : t + y ∈ A}) dHⁿ(t) (Measure.map_apply, Measure.prod_apply).
Rectangles p⁻¹A ∩ q⁻¹B form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra, because y = p y + q y.

Because σ is carried by V^⊥, λ(p⁻¹A ∩ q⁻¹B) = σ(B)·Hⁿ(A ∩ V) = ν(p⁻¹A ∩ q⁻¹B); the rectangles p⁻¹B_j(0) ∩ q⁻¹B_j(0) cover ℝ^P with finite ν-measure (subspace_ball), so ν = λ by uniqueness of measures (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion).
